title: Identity Before Design
definition: A visual or verbal decision is valid only when it expresses a previously defined identity commitment. Design cannot compensate for an unresolved promise, audience, position or behavior; it can only make that ambiguity more visible.
when_to_use: When a brand redesign lacks a strategic reason
diagnostic_method: Link each design decision to that commitment
Reject or revise decisions without a traceable link
observable_indicators: Every major asset cites an identity commitment
Design reviews use identity criteria instead of personal taste
analysis_questions: What identity commitment does this decision express?
What would change if the commitment were different?
Is the choice strategic or merely decorative?
decision_rules: Do not approve an asset without an identity rationale
When two options are equally attractive, select the one with stronger identity traceability

good_examples.situation: A premium travel brand removes visual noise because calm authority is part of its identity
good_examples.result: The design choice reinforces a declared positioning

bad_examples.situation: A brand adopts neon gradients only because they are trending

limits_and_counterexamples: Exploratory sketches may precede final identity decisions
Functional accessibility requirements override stylistic preferences
expected_result: Identity decisions become explicit constraints that guide design and reduce arbitrary revisions.

relationships.justification: Identity commitments need perceptual translation to become visible before explanation.

forbidden_uses: Treating the candidate as approved canon
Using it as evidence of a real-world fact without an external source

review_note: Aprobado por el fundador para el canon piloto Entity Bible v2.
